full_judgment:
4. The plaintiff-opposite parties examined 4 PWs and the defendant-petitioners, on the other hand, examined 2 DWs in support of their respective case. During the trial the plaintiff-opposite parties proved and exhibited SA and RS Khatians and the defendant-petitioner filed and proved relevant documents showing that there was a mortgage suit and the suit land was subsequently purchased in auction-sale by them in execution of a mortgage decree by filing an execution case and got possession thereof. 

 6. On an appeal by the plaintiff-opposite parties the appellate Court below decreed the suit by reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court only on point of law namely, that the order of mutation passed by the revenue authority in 1969 under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in favour of the defendant-petitioners setting aside the entries in the SA Khatian was without jurisdiction and was thus liable to be set aside. 

 7. Mr Abdul Quayum, learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners, submits that since the instant suit is not maintainable being hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, the trial Court rightly dismissed the same and the appellate Court below committed an error of law by decreeing the same when it was liable to be dismissed in limini. The learned Advocate elaborating his augment submits that the plaintiff-opposite parties had no locus standi to file the present suit inasmuch as they could not be said to have any legal character or right to property in respect of the suit land inasmuch as SA Khatian standing in their names had no presumptive value as regards proprietary right to the suit land. It is also contended by the learned Advocate that the suit is not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as the plaintiff-opposite parties failed to seek any declaration as to their own status and also failed to pray for a further or consequential relief by way of possession. In support of his aforesaid submissions the learned Advocate referred to and relied on the cases reported in 18 DLR 706, to show that the plaintiff must have legal character or right to property, 6 BCR (AD) 57 showing that mere declaration in the absence of consequential relief is fatal, 42 DLR 24 and 13 DLR 676 showing that symbolical possession by defendant requires plaintiff to seek relief for recovery of possession. The learned Advocate also relied on the case reported in 19 DLR 9 in support of his contention that the SA Khatian does not give rise to any presumption of title to the suit land. 

 9. Admittedly, both the SA Khatians as well as RS Khatians in respect of the suit land stand in the names of the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiff-opposite parties and also in some of their names. It is true that the SA records, in view of section 19(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, do not provide conclusive evidence as regards title but it provides conclusive evidence as regards their preparation and revision. But entries in the SA records; in my opinion, provide a prima facie evidence as regards title. In order to maintain a suit for declaration under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, the plaintiff is required to have prima facie evidence showing that he has a legal character or right to a property in respect of the subject matter of the suit and granting or refusal to grant a decree in such suit shall always depend on final adjudication thereof on evidence. Since the SA records vide Exts 3 and 3(Ka) stand in the names of the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff-opposite parties and also in some of their names it should be taken to be a prima facie evidence of title of the plaintiff-opposite parties in respect of the suit land and, as such, the plaintiff-opposite parties were competent to file the present suit. I do not dispute the legal principles deduced in the aforesaid cases cited by the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners. Since the present suit was not for a declaration of title but for a declaration of the act of the revenue authority namely, the order of mutation outside the purview of law as illegal the same is certainly maintainable. Reference may be made in this connection to the case reported in 16 DLR 298.
